==Biography==
===Season 3===
Lee "'''Faker'''" Sang-hyeok was pulled out of solo queue by the SK Telecom organization so that a team could be formed around him in the mid lane. Ultimately they settled on [[Impact]], [[bengi]], [[Piglet]], and [[PoohManDu]] to surround him and the team was unveiled in February of 2013, dubbed [[SK Telecom T1 2]]. They qualified for their first OGN at [[OLYMPUS Champions Spring 2013]]. They exceeded all expectations and placed 3rd, losing 3-1 in the semifinals to [[MVP Ozone]] but beating [[CJ Entus Frost]] 3-0 in the third-place match. Faker's dominating performances put him in the conversation for best mid laner in the world after just one tournament. The team was renamed to [[SK Telecom T1]] after their sister team, [[SK Telecom T1 1]], was disbanded. With a great first result under their belts, they attended [[HOT6iX Champions Summer 2013]]. Faker continued his fantastic play and led his team to a reverse sweep of the [[KT Rolster Bullets]] and earned them a berth at the [[Season 3 Korea Regional Finals]]. They were seeded directly into the finals and met the Bullets again, only to soundly beat them 3-1. SK Telecom qualified for the [[Season 3 World Championship]] as the final Korean seed but still came in as the favorites to win the whole tournament. Faker crushed the competition and the team put up an impressive 15-3 record across the tournament, culminating in a one-sided final where they beat [[Royal Club]] 3-0 and became the new world champions. Faker's brilliant play across the season earned him the title of the best player in the world by most fans and experts alike. The SK Telecom organization picked up a new sister team, ultimately named [[SK Telecom T1 S]], so Faker's team was renamed to SK Telecom T1 K.

===2014 Season===
The new season started even better for K at [[PANDORA.TV Champions Winter 2013-2014]]. They didn't lose a single game and put up the greatest performance a team has ever had at an OGN tournament. They swept [[Samsung Ozone]] in the finals and Faker proved himself as the greatest LoL player of all time after just a year. However, the success wasn't meant to last after ManDu stepped down due to health issues and the team picked up [[Casper (Kwon Ji-min)|Casper]]. An ultimately poor showing at [[HOT6iX Champions Spring 2014]] was capped off with a 3-1 loss to Ozone in the quarterfinals. ManDu rejoined the starting line up before [[All-Star Paris 2014]], where the team was expected to falter. In typical fashion, they swept the whole tournament and earned a clean 9-0 record, ending in a dominating final against [[OMG]]. They returned to Korea with high hopes to participate in [[HOT6iX Champions Summer 2014]] but ended up mirroring the results of their last OGN, losing 3-1 in the quarterfinals to Samsung White. They lost in a tiebreaker for the 2nd Korean seed to worlds, again to White, by being swept. K was seeded into the finals of the [[2014 Season Korea Regional Finals]] but ended up losing 3-1 to [[NaJin White Shield]] and missed [[2014 Season World Championship|Worlds]].

===2015 Season===
Changes to the OGN rules forced K and S to merge, forming SK Telecom T1. Most of the old K roster was removed, except for Bengi and Faker, while [[MaRin]], [[Wolf (Lee Jae-wan)|Wolf]], and [[Bang]] filled out the rest of the line-up. [[Easyhoon]] and Faker shared the starting mid lane spot for [[SBENU Champions Spring 2015]], to the disappointment of many fans who wanted to see Faker play in every game. Despite SK Telecom's strong performance in the informal [[Champions Spring 2015/Preseason|Spring Preseason]], they were not the top team in the season itself, and it was the newly-formed [[GE Tigers]] who were invited to [[IEM Season IX - World Championship|IEM Katowice]] as the top team from Korea, not SKT. And SKT finished second in the season overall, with an 11-3 record - one game behind the Tigers. Regardless, in the [[SBENU Champions Spring 2015/Playoffs|playoffs]], SKT beat both CJ Entus and the Tigers - without Faker even starting for a single game against the Tigers.

Their spring season championship qualified SK Telecom for the [[2015 Mid-Season Invitational]]. There, they swept the group stage 5-0 but then dropped two games to the European [[Fnatic]] in the semifinals, beating them 3-2, with Faker starting each game. In the finals against [[EDward Gaming]], Easyhoon started for the first three games, and SKT ultimately lost 3-2. In the final game of the set, EDG famously left open [[LeBlanc]] for Faker - a champion he was until then undefeated on - and counterpicked it with a mid lane [[Morgana]] for [[pawN]], running a composition designed to shut down Faker.

After the Mid-Season Invitational, SKT bounced back and won the regular season of [[SBENU Champions Summer 2015|Champions Summer]], dropping only one set along the way - though it was the set that would have made them the first team worldwide to clinch a [[2015 Season World Championship|Worlds]] seed (they ended up clinching their seed when the GE Tigers lost their very next set as well). Faker played 12 unique champions in his 29 games, innovating mid lane [[Irelia]], a pick that would become a relatively popular off-meta pick around the world, and [[Master Yi]], a pick that would not. Seeded directly into the [[SBENU Champions Summer 2015/Playoffs|playoff finals]] this time, SKT easily swept KT Rolster 3-0 (Faker played all three games) to earn Korea's top seed to the [[2015 Season World Championship]]. SKT was placed in a group at worlds alongside EDG, [[Bangkok Titans]], and [[H2k Gaming]]. They went undefeated all the way to the finals, beating [[AHQ e-Sports Club]] and [[Origen]] in the playoffs along the way. They met the KOO Tigers in the finals and beat them 3-1 to give the organization its second World Championship. This made Faker one of only three people (the other two being his coach [[kkOma]] and Bengi) to have won the World Championship twice.

===2016 Season===
Two weeks after the World Championship, SK Telecom played in the [[2015 LoL KeSPA Cup|LoL KeSPA Cup]]. In their semifinal series against Challenger team [[ESC Ever|Ever]], substitute mid laner [[Scout]] started in the first game, but even with Faker playing in the second game, the team lost the series 0-2 - continuing a streak of World Champions being eliminated early on in their first tournaments after Worlds. SK Telecom announced Faker's re-signing for the 2016 season after the tournament.<ref>[http://osen.mt.co.kr/article/G1110294253 <nowiki>[단독] '페이커' 이상혁, 소속팀 SK텔레콤과 재계약  (Korean)</nowiki>] ''osen.mt.co.kr''</ref> In March, SK Telecom attended [[IEM Season X - World Championship|IEM Katowice]] despite being only the sixth-place [[LCK/2016 Season/Spring Season|LCK]] team at the time. They brought substitute jungler [[Blank (Kang Sun-gu)|Blank]] in place of Bengi and swept through the tournament, winning the title after only seven games. After returning to Korea, a rejuvenated Faker helped the team climb back up the standings and eventually win his fifth Korean championship and third consecutive title. This win allowed SKT to return to the Mid Season Invitational, the only team to return from the previous year.

Their first-place finish in the [[LCK/2016 Season/Spring Season|spring season]] earned them a spot in the [[2016 Mid-Season Invitational]]. Notably, SK Telecom T1 was the only team to return to 2016 MSI from [[2015 Mid-Season Invitational|2015 MSI]]. As the reigning domestic champions of Korea, SK Telecom T1 came into the tournament as massive favorites to win. However, their group stage performances were very lackluster as they dropped games to China's [[Royal Never Give Up]], NA's [[Counter Logic Gaming]], and two games to the LMS [[Flash Wolves]]. They ended their group stage with a 6-4 record, seeding them into the bracket stage in fourth place. Matched up against [[Royal Never Give Up]] in the semifinals, SK Telecom started to regain their form, beating them 3-1. They then proceeded to beat [[Counter Logic Gaming]] 3-0 to win the event and give them the trophy that barely escaped them last year.

During the [[LCK/2016 Season/Summer Season|2016 LCK Summer Split]], SK Telecom started the season strong with a 5-0 score in series and a 10-0 game score. However, they started dropping sets to lower-ranked teams, notably the [[Afreeca Freecs]], who failed to win even a single game against the entire season. With a 13-5 scoreline in series, SKT placed second in the round-robin, beating [[KT Rolster]] via game score tiebreaker. However, during the [[LCK/2016 Season/Summer Playoffs|2016 LCK Summer Playoffs]], they met [[KT Rolster]] in the semifinals, where they were reverse swept 3-2 after going up 2-0 in the first two games. This gave them a third place for the summer split. Combined with their first-place spring finish, as well as the victory of the [[ROX Tigers]] over [[KT Rolster]], SKT qualified to the [[2016 Season World Championship]] on points as Korea's second seed.

At the [[2016 Season World Championship]], SK Telecom T1 was placed into Group B, along with LMS's [[Flash Wolves]], NA's [[Cloud 9]], and China's [[I May]].

Notable Achievements=
=== Notable Achievements ===
* Dubbed the "Unkillable Demon King" by [[Cool]] during a pre-game interview during [[Worlds 2013]], which has become a widely used title for him.<ref>[http://www.youtube.com/watch?feature=player_embedded&v=fPyJES5-vAo#t=32965 Worlds 2013 Group Stage Day 6] ''youtube.com''</ref>
* Is highly regarded for his {{ci|LeBlanc}} play during an OGN Spring match against [[MVP Blue]]; he went 10-0-1 by 18 minutes and made MVP Blue surrender at 20 minutes.<ref>[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m2tTkQzWcqA Legendary Faker_LOL Champs Spring Highlight Ep.7_Match2] ''youtube.com''</ref>
* Solo-killed [[Ambition]]'s {{ci|Khazix}} during his debut in OGN. At the time Ambition was considered as one of the best mid laners in Korea.
* Was undefeated on {{ci|LeBlanc}} until the [[2015 Mid-Season Invitational]] final against [[EDward Gaming]], where he lost with LeBlanc in Game 5.
* He is considered the best League of Legends player in the world by many esports journalists and pro players such as [[Thorin]], [[Alex Ich]], and [[Maknoon]] who called him the "Lionel Messi of League of Legends".<ref>[http://na.lolesports.com/articles/experts-weigh-worlds-predictions-1 Experts weigh in with Worlds predictions] ''na.lolesports.com''</ref><ref>[http://cloth5.com/an-interview-with-gambit-gamings-alex_ich <nowiki>Interview with Alex Ich: "[Faker's] skill level is over the edge at the moment"</nowiki>] ''cloth5.com''</ref>
* Dustin Beck, the vice president of Riot Games, said Faker is the "Michael Jordan" of League of Legends in a press conference at Staples Center.<ref>[http://www.inven.co.kr/webzine/news/?news=64531 <nowiki>[2013 롤드컵] '페이커'는 LOL의 마이클 조던… 라이엇게임즈 임원진 공동 인터뷰 (Korean)</nowiki>] ''inven.co.kr''</ref>
* In the first game of the 2013 OGN summer championships, Faker played Ahri and scored a GPM of 492.
* Was both the Season MVP and the Mid Lane KDA leader in the [[HOT6iX Champions Summer 2013]].
* Known for his amazing solo queue performance with {{ci|Riven}} on the North American server during the [[Season 3 World Championship]], earning him a 92 % win rate in 24 games.
* Known for his stellar performance with {{ci|Ryze}} during [[2015 Season World Championship]] and {{ci|Galio}} during [[2017 Season World Championship]].
* Popularized {{ci|Riven}} being played in the mid lane.
* Awarded Best Mid Laner at 2013 Korean eSports Awards.<ref>[http://www.inven.co.kr/webzine/news/?news=103849 <nowiki>[e스포츠 대상] 최강의 LoL 팀 SK텔레콤 T1 K, 영광의 대상 차지(종합) (Korean)</nowiki>] ''inven.com.kr''</ref>
* One of eight players to have defended their World Championship successfully (with [[Bengi]], [[Bang]], [[Wolf (Lee Jae-wan)|Wolf]], [[Zeus]], [[Oner]], [[Gumayusi]], [[Keria]]), the only one to have done it twice.
** He is the only player to have won World Championship six times (2013, 2015, 2016, 2023, 2024, 2025).
* Has the highest number of appearances in finals in the history of the World Championship, with 8 in total (2013, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025).
* Has the highest number of appearances in finals in the history of the Mid-Season Invitational, with 5 in total (2015, 2016, 2017, 2022, and 2025).
* He is the oldest player to ever win the World Championship, at 29 years, 6 months, and 2 days.
* As of 2024, he has the longest continuous tenure of any player with a single organization.
* With 10 LCK titles, he is the player with the most LCK titles in the entire LCK's history, from the first in Summer 2013 to the tenth in Spring 2022.
* He is the winner of the "''Esports PC Player of the Year''" prize at the Esports Awards in 2023 and 2024.<ref>[https://x.com/esportsawards/status/1730387319730172372 Esports Awards' X Post] ''x.com''</ref>
* He is the winner of the "''Esports PC Player of the Decade''" prize at the Esports Awards in 2025.
* His 10th-anniversary documentary named "Faker: A Decade of Greatness" produced by Riot Games earned the "''Esports Content of the Year''" at the Esports Awards 2023. <ref> [https://youtu.be/wU-1ZaT0hIg?si=gwgQir9meVwOYTIV LoL Esports] </ref><ref> [https://x.com/esportsawards/status/1730387319730172372?s=20 Esports Awards' X Post] ''x.com''</ref>
* He is the winner of the "''Best Esports Athlete''" award at The Game Awards in 2017, 2023 and 2024.<ref>[https://thegameawards.com/nominees/best-esports-athlete Official 'Game Awards' Website] ''thegameawards.com''</ref>
* He is the first player to have been awarded the Worlds MVP twice.

Statistics=
=== Statistics ===
==== International ====
* Reached 500 international kills during [[2019 Mid-Season Invitational|MSI 2019]] on May 18th, 2019 in Semifinals, becoming the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 1000 international kills during [[2025 Mid-Season Invitational|MSI 2025]] on July 10th, 2025 in Upper Finals, becoming the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 100 international wins during [[Worlds 2019 Main Event|Worlds 2019]] on October 27th, 2019 after SK Telecom's second victory against [[Splyce]] in the quarterfinals, becoming the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 200 international wins during [[2025 Mid-Season Invitational|MSI 2025]] on July 6th, 2025 after T1's second victory against [[Bilibili Gaming]] in round 2 of stage 2, becoming the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 200 international games during [[2023 Mid-Season Invitational|MSI 2023]] on May 10th, 2023 in T1's second game against [[MAD Lions KOI]] in Round 1, becoming the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 300 international games during [[Worlds 2025 Main Event|Worlds 2025]] on October 15th, 2025 in T1's game against [[Flyquest]] in Swiss Round 1, becoming the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 1000 international assists during [[Worlds 2022 Main Event|Worlds 2022]] on October 21st, 2022 against [[RNG]] in Quarterfinals, becoming the 2nd player to achieve this milestone after [[Ming (Shi Sen-Ming)|Ming]].
* Reached 100 wins in [[World Championship]] on October 11th, 2024, becoming the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 500 kills at [[Worlds]] on November 2nd, 2024 in game 4 of the [[2024 Season World Championship | Final]] against [[BLG]], as the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 1000 assists at [[Worlds]] on November 9th, 2025 in game 5 of the [[2025 Season World Championship | Final]] against [[KT Rolster]], as the 1st player to achieve this milestone.
* Reached 500 kills at [[MSI]] on July 10th, 2025 in game 4 of the [[2025 Mid-Season Invitational|MSI 2025]] against [[GEN]], as the 1st player to achieve this milestone.

==== LCK ====
* Reached 1000 kills in the LCK on July 11th, 2016.<ref>[https://www.akshonesports.com/article/2016/07/faker-sets-a-new-record-1000-kills-in-the-lck-interview-translated Faker Sets A New Record - First Player To Reach 1,000 Kills In the LCK] ''akshonesports.com''</ref>
** The 1st player to reach 1000 kills in the LCK.
